claims.claim: Cyril of Jerusalem, who served as Archbishop (bishop) of Jerusalem, is the author of the Homily on the Meeting of the Lord.
Cyril lived circa 313–386 AD and became bishop of Jerusalem around 350 AD.
The homily exists in Greek and was later translated into Coptic, Arabic, Ethiopic (three manuscripts, the oldest from the 14th century), and Slavonic.
The Greek text is preserved in Patrologia Graeca volume 33 (pages 1188‑1204) and has been printed in modern editions.
The homily is considered apocryphal in some traditions, yet it is valued for its insight into 4th‑century liturgical practice and theology of the Presentation.

The homily is one of the earliest surviving homilies on the Presentation and is cited among the great feast sermons of early church fathers such as Methodius, Gregory the Theologian, and John Chrysostom.
